title: BIS Quarterly Review, March 2026 - International banking and financial market developments
summary: The BIS Quarterly Review for March 2026 examines global financial market developments, highlighting how markets are recalibrating amid geopolitical tensions while selective risk-taking continues. Key market structure topics include the rise of synthetic risk transfers (SRTs) as a mechanism for distributing credit risk, offshore activity patterns in international banking, and the intersection of private credit with AI infrastructure financing. The publication also introduces BISTRO, a large language model-based oracle for macroeconomic time series forecasting.
key_points: Synthetic risk transfers (SRTs) have emerged as a growing market for distributing credit risk, with the review providing economics, market trends, and system-wide risk assessment of this market structure
The AI infrastructure boom is being financed through both on- and off-balance sheet borrowing, with Box A analyzing these financing patterns
Private credit's software lending is intersecting with AI disruption, as detailed in Box B examining this evolving market structure
Leveraged retail investors played a role in the boom and bust dynamics of recent silver and gold markets (Box C)
Sovereign bond markets have diverged amid changing monetary and fiscal policy outlooks globally
Offshore activity analysis reveals patterns in cross-border banking and non-bank financial intermediation (NBFIs)
BISTRO is introduced as a foundational language model for macroeconomic time series forecasting, representing financial data infrastructure innovation
